questions.question: The first modern Olympic Games was held in the year ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1896.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• ** The International Olympic Committee (IOC) was founded in 1894, and it was decided that the first modern Olympic Games would be held two years later in Athens, Greece.**
 
• The first modern Olympic Games were held from **April 6 to April 15, 1896, and featured 14 nations and 241 athletes competing in 43 events.**
 
• The Games were a huge success and helped to revive the ancient tradition of** Olympic competition, which had been dormant for more than 1,500 years.**
 
• The modern Olympic Games have been held every four years since 1896, with the exception of 1916, 1940, and 1944 due to World War I and II.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• The Olympic flag has a white background, with five interlaced rings in the centre: blue, yellow, black, green, and red.

 
 
• Each colour corresponds to a particular continent: blue for Europe, yellow for Asia, black for Africa, green for Australia and Oceania, and red for the Americas.
 
 
 
• The Olympic motto “Citius, Altius, Fortius” (“Faster, Higher, Stronger”) was coined by Father Henri Didon.
 
• Only three modern Olympic Games have been cancelled.
 
 
• The games were cancelled due to World War I (1914) and World War II (1940, 1944).
 
 
 
• The youngest Olympian is Greek gymnast Dimitrios Loundras, who competed in the 1896 Athens Olympics at the age of 10.

questions.question: In which month of the Islamic calendar is 'Ramadan', a holy time when Muslims around the world fast and focus their attention on giving to charity (known as Zakat), observed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ninth.**__

__
 
• **The correct answer is option 1, i.e., the ninth month of the Islamic calendar is Ramadan.**
 
• Ramadan is considered one of the **holiest months in the Islamic calendar,** during which Muslims fast from dawn to dusk and engage in spiritual reflection and acts of charity.
 
• Ramadan is a time of spiritual growth and self-discipline for Muslims worldwide, and it is believed to be a time when the gates of heaven are open, and the gates of hell are closed.
 
• During Ramadan, Muslims are required to abstain from food, drink, and other physical needs during daylight hours, and they are encouraged to engage in acts of charity, prayer, and good deeds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Radhe Sham Barle received the Padma Shri in 2020-21 for promoting the Panthi dance of tribals from the Santnami community on the birth anniversary of Guru Ghasidas. Which state does this dance form belong to?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Chhattisgarh.**__

__
 
• **The correct answer is option 2, Chhattisgarh.**
 
• Panthi dance is a **traditional folk dance of the Santnami community of Chhattisgarh.**
 
• This dance form is performed on the occasion of **Guru Ghasidas Jayanti, which is celebrated in honor of the founder of the Satnami sect.**
 
• The dance is characterized by its rhythmic movements and **foot-tapping beats, accompanied by the melodious sound of the 'manjiras' and 'dholak'.**
 
• The dance is performed by both men and women and is a popular form of entertainment in rural areas of Chhattisgarh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Madhya Pradesh **- Madhya Pradesh has its own traditional folk dances like** Gond, Bhilala, and Baiga.**
 
• ** Odisha **- Odisha has its own traditional folk dances like **Ghumura, Sambalpuri, and Dalkhai.**

questions.question: Padma Shri awardee, Darshana Jhaveri is a ______ dancer of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Manipuri.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **The correct answer to the question is option 4, Manipuri.**

 
 
• **Darshana Jhaveri is a renowned Manipuri dancer** from India who has been awarded the Padma Shri in 2007 for her contribution to the field of dance.
 
• Manipuri is a classical dance form that originated in the northeastern state of Manipur in India and is known for its graceful movements, delicate footwork, and storytelling through dance.
 
 
 
• Bharatanatyam is another popular classical dance form from South India that is characterized by intricate footwork, hand gestures, and facial expressions. It is known for its dynamic and rhythmic movements.
 
• Kathak is a North Indian classical dance form that emphasizes fast spins, footwork, and storytelling through dance. It is known for its intricate rhythmic patterns and graceful movements.
 
• Kathakali is a traditional dance-drama form from the southern state of Kerala that combines dance, music, and acting. It is known for its elaborate costumes, makeup, and facial expressions that are used to convey emotions and tell stories.
 
• Hence, the statement "Padma Shri awardee, Darshana Jhaveri is a Manipuri dancer of India" is correct.

questions.question: Which of the following trade agreements aims to 'strengthen intra-SAARC economic cooperation to maximise the region's potential for trade and achieving development for their people'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** SAFTA.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **SAFTA stands for South Asian Free Trade Area and is a trade agreement among the member states of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC).**

 
 
• SAFTA was signed in **2004 and came into effect in 2006 with the aim to promote and enhance trade and economic cooperation among the SAARC countries.**
 
• SAFTA aims to **reduce and eliminate tariffs and non-tariff barriers **on goods traded within the region, and to address other issues related to trade in services and investment.
 
• SAFTA also includes provisions for safeguard measures to protect domestic industries from sudden surges in imports from other member countries.
 
 
 
• APTA (Asia-Pacific Trade Agreement) is a trade agreement among six countries in the Asia-Pacific region, while NAFTA (North American Free Trade Agreement) is a trade agreement between the United States, Canada, and Mexico, and LAIA (Latin American Integration Association) is a regional trade bloc in Latin America.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 2, SAFTA.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India enshrines to value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture?
Chandragupta Maurya overthrew the Nanda Dynasty of Magadha with the help of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Vishnugupta.**__

__
 
• **Chandragupta Maurya overthrew the Nanda Dynasty of Magadha with the help of Vishnugupta, who is also known as Chanakya.**
 
• Chanakya was a wise and learned scholar who played a crucial role in the rise of the **Mauryan Empire**.
 
• He was the chief advisor to** Chandragupta Maurya and helped him in his conquests and administrative policies.**
 
• It is believed that Chanakya wrote the famous book Arthashastra, which deals with economics, politics, and governance.
 
• With the help of Chanakya, Chandragupta Maurya was able to defeat the powerful Nanda Dynasty and establish the Mauryan Empire, which became one of the greatest empires in ancient India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Skandagupta** was a **Gupta Emperor who ruled from 455 to 467 CE.**
 
• He was known for his military campaigns against the Huns.
 
• Chandragupta II, also known as** Vikramaditya, was a Gupta Emperor who ruled from 380 to 415 CE.** He was known for his patronage of art and literature.
 
• Samudragupta was a Gupta Emperor who ruled from **335 to 375 CE.**
 
• He was known for **his military campaigns and conquests.**

questions.question: Which of the following is also known as the 'lender of the last resort'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**RBI.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The correct answer is option 3, RBI, which is also known as the 'lender of the last resort'.**
 
• The lender of the last resort is a term used to **describe an institution that provides emergency funds** to other financial institutions when they are facing a shortage of liquidity.
 
• This is usually done to prevent a financial crisis or a bank run.
 
• In India, th**e Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is the lender of the last resort**.
 
• It has the authority to lend money to banks and other financial institutions in case of a crisis.
 
• The RBI also acts as the regulator of the banking system in India. It sets policies and guidelines for banks to follow, and monitors their performance to ensure that they are operating in a safe and sound manner.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **SEBI(Securities Exchange Board of India)** is the regulator of the securities market in India. It does not have the authority to lend money to financial institutions.
 
• **RRBs (Regional Rural Banks)** are a type of bank that focuses on providing banking services to the rural population. They do not have the authority to act as the lender of the last resort.
 
• ** SBI (State Bank of India)** is a public sector bank in India. While it is one of the largest banks in the country, it does not have the authority to act as the lender of the last resort.

questions.question: Which of the following acids makes up 55-80% of olive oil, making it a good choice for most cooking methods?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Oleic acid.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• ** The correct answer is option 2, which is Oleic acid.**

 
 
• **Oleic acid is a monounsaturated omega-9 fatty acid that is found in high quantities in olive oil.**
 
• This acid has a **high smoke point,** which makes it a good choice for most cooking methods, including frying and baking.
 
• It is also known for its** health benefits, such as reducing inflammation and improving heart health.**
 
 
 
• Lauric acid (option 1) is a saturated fatty acid found in** coconut oil and palm kernel oil **and is known for its antimicrobial properties.
 
• Arachidic acid (option 3) is a saturated fatty acid found in peanut oil and other vegetable oils.
 
• Stearic acid (option 4) is a saturated fatty acid that is found in animal fats and some vegetable oils.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer to the question is option 2, Oleic acid, which makes up 55-80% of olive oil and is a good choice for most cooking methods.

questions.question: What is an instrument that sends pulses of electromagnetic energy into the atmosphere to detect rainfall, determine its speed and intensity, and identify precipitation types such as rain, snow or hail?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Doppler weather radar.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The correct instrument is the Doppler weather radar, which is used for the detection of rainfall and precipitation types.**
 
• Doppler weather radar uses** pulses of electromagnetic energy to detect precipitation in the atmosphere.**
 
• It can determine the speed and intensity of** rainfall, and identify different types of precipitation such as rain, snow, or hail.**
 
• Doppler weather radar is a critical tool for weather forecasting and warning systems, as it provides real-time data on precipitation patterns and can help predict severe weather events.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Barometer** is a tool used to** measure atmospheric pressure** and is not used to detect precipitation.
 
• **A spectral pyranometer** is used to **measure solar radiation** and is not used for detecting precipitation.
 
• **A 2D sonic anemometer** is used to **measure wind speed and direction** and is not used for detecting precipitation.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding Parliamentary Committees?

A. A minister cannot be a member of the Public Accounts Committee.

B. The members of the Estimates Committee are nominated by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

C. A minister can be a member of the Estimates Committee if he is nominated by the Speaker.

D. A member of the Committee on Public Undertakings will have tenure of 2 years.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** A only.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• Parliamentary Committees are formed to assist the Parliament in its work.
 
• **There are three types of Parliamentary Committees - Standing Committees, Select Committees, and Joint Committees.**
 
• The members of these Committees are elected or** nominated by the Parliament or its Speaker.**
 
• ** Statement A is correct.**
 
 
• According to the rules, a minister cannot be a member of the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) as it is an oversight committee that examines the government's expenditures.
 
 
 
• ** Statement B is incorrect.**
 
 
• **​** The members of the Estimates Committee are not nominated by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha. They are elected by the Lok Sabha from among its members.
 
 
 
• ** Statement C is incorrect. **
 
 
• **​**A minister cannot be a member of the Estimates Committee even if he is nominated by the Speaker.
 
 
 
• ** Statement D is incorrect.**
 
 
• **​** The tenure of a member of the Committee on Public Undertakings is one year.
 
 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) is the oldest and most important Parliamentary Committee.
 
• The Estimates Committee examines the estimates of expenditure of various ministries.
 
• The Committee on Public Undertakings examines the working of government-owned companies.

questions.question: The famous Arabic scholar Al Biruni came to contact with India through ______ in the eleventh century A.D.

• He wrote several books on these topics, including **"The Book of India," which is considered one of the most important works on Indian culture and history.**
 
• ** Al Biruni's work had a significant impact on both Indian and Islamic scholarship**, and his legacy continues to this day. He is remembered as one of the greatest scholars of the Islamic Golden Age.

• Muhammad Bin Qasim was an Arab general who led the Umayyad conquest of Sindh in 711 A.D. He is known for his military exploits but had no direct connection to Al Biruni or his work.

questions.question: 'A Plan of Economic Development for India' is also known as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** the Bombay Plan.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **The correct answer is option 4, i.e., Bombay Plan**.
 
• Bombay Plan was a **set of proposals for the economic development of India**, presented by a group of leading industrialists and economists in 1944.
 
• It was named after the city where it was drafted, i.e., Bombay (now Mumbai).
 
• The plan **aimed to create a mixed economy in India**, with a balance between the public and private sectors.
 
• It called for an increase in public investment in key sectors such as agriculture, industry, and infrastructure, while also promoting entrepreneurship and free enterprise.
 
• The Bombay Plan was seen as a response to the challenge o**f post-war reconstruction and development in India, as well as a critique of the laissez-faire policies of the colonial government.**
 
• It was also influenced by socialist and Fabian ideas, as well as the experience of planned economies in other countries.
 
• The Bombay Plan received both praise and criticism from different quarters. Some saw it as a visionary blueprint for India's future, while others criticized it as elitist, impractical, or insufficiently radical. However, it remains an important landmark in the history of economic thought and policy in India.
 
• The other options mentioned in the question are not correct because they do not refer to any actual plan of economic development for India. Delhi, Gujarat, and Surat are all cities or states in India, but they do not have any such plans named after them. Therefore, option 4, i.e., Bombay Plan, is the correct answer.
